references.text: The Lord sets a specific time (מוֹעֵד) for when the plague will occur, just as in Exodus 9:5 where the Lord establishes the timing of the livestock pestilence.
The Lord again sets a specific time ('tomorrow') for when the hail plague will come, following the same pattern of advance warning.
Moses warns that the locust plague will come 'tomorrow' (מָחָר), the same word used to indicate the timing of God's action.
The Lord announces in advance that the final plague will happen, demonstrating God's sovereignty over the timing of His judgments.
The Lord sets a specific time (מוֹעֵד) for His action, showing His power to determine when His will shall be fulfilled.
The Lord sets a specific time for victory, showing that God controls the timings of His actions in history.
Direct linguistic and thematic parallel: God's use of 'tomorrow' to confirm that His word is immediately put into action.
Strong thematic parallel: God's use of 'tomorrow' to reveal His will and distinguish between the holy and the rebellious.
Theological parallel concerning God's sovereign control over time: His word is fulfilled without delay on the appointed day.
